title: Insurance Coverage & Claims Registration Policy: Coverages on File per Patient
content:
**Insurance Coverage & Claims** — the number of health-plan coverages a patient may keep on file with Halverson Clinical Laboratories, and when a coverage may be put on file again.

## Clauses

1. **Limit.** A patient may have at most 3 coverages on file that are not terminated, one per payment position: primary, secondary and tertiary.
2. **Terminated coverages.** Terminated coverages stay on file without limit and do not count toward the 3.
3. **Fourth live coverage.** A fourth live coverage is refused until one of the patient's live coverages is terminated.
4. **Same payer and member ID.** The same payer and member ID may not be on file twice while the earlier record is not terminated: a correction to a live record is made on that record.

## What the clauses read

- A coverage is *live* (not terminated) while its status is pending verification, active or inactive.
- Clause 4 is decided from the coverage records on file, not from the caller's account: the payer name and member ID of the coverage being put on file are compared with the payer name, member ID and status of the patient's existing coverage records. The object compared is the pair of payer and member ID together.

## Cases (hypothetical patients)

| Coverages already on file | Coverage to be put on file | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Two active, one terminated | A third live coverage with a new payer | Within the limit: 2 live coverages become 3 |
| One active, one pending verification, one inactive | Any further coverage | Refused until one of the three is terminated |
| One inactive record with Payer A, member ID 123 | Payer A, member ID 123 | Not put on file twice: the correction is made on the inactive record |
| One terminated record with Payer A, member ID 123 | Payer A, member ID 123 | Clause 4 does not bar it: the earlier record is terminated |
| One active record with Payer A, member ID 123 | Payer B, member ID 123 | Clause 4 does not bar it: the payer differs |
